📌 Watch-Only Wallets: Tracking Crypto Without Access to Funds

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

Trump Eyes a New War With Iran


Trump has received a high-level military briefing on potential U.S. military action against Iran, raising fresh questions about whether Washington is preparing to resume major combat operations in the Middle East after the November 3 midterm elections.

Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), met with Trump at the White House on Thursday to discuss possible military options involving Iran. The unusual face-to-face meeting also included Defense Secretary Hegseth, Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine and other senior administration officials, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing U.S. officials and people familiar with the discussions.

The meeting comes as the Trump administration weighs its next move in an increasingly volatile confrontation with Tehran. U.S. officials have reportedly warned several Arab Gulf nations to prepare for a potentially short but intense military campaign after the midterm elections. 

The possible targets could include Iranian military infrastructure and nuclear facilities, according to separate reporting by the Associated Press.Trump has publicly left the door open to renewed military action, suggesting that Washington could launch another limited campaign if Iran refuses to accept U.S. demands. 

Speaking at a rally last week, the president referred to the possibility of another operation similar to the U.S.-Israeli bombing campaign conducted earlier this year, known as Operation Epic Fury.

The administration has also strengthened its military posture across the region. The Pentagon has reinforced air defenses, increased supplies of ammunition and other military equipment, and taken steps to reduce the vulnerability of American personnel at exposed bases. An additional Patriot missile battery is also being sent to Israel as regional forces face growing pressure on their air-defense resources.

Meanwhile, Iran has signaled that any new American attack could trigger retaliation against U.S. and Gulf targets. Tehran has reportedly resumed ballistic missile production and intensified efforts to threaten American personnel and regional military installations. Thursday's White House meeting followed another high-level session on Wednesday, when senior military officials met with JD Vance. 

The sequence of briefings underscores the growing attention within the administration to possible military scenarios involving Iran. However, a presidential briefing does not mean that a decision to launch new strikes has been made. Diplomacy remains an option, and officials familiar with the discussions have indicated that Trump has not given final approval for another military operation.

The timing is particularly significant. With the November 3 elections approaching, Trump faces competing pressures: maintaining his campaign promise to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon while avoiding a wider regional conflict that could carry substantial military, economic and political costs. 

For now, Washington appears to be keeping both military and diplomatic options on the table. Whether the latest White House consultations lead to renewed strikes or become another round of strategic pressure on Tehran remains an open question.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
